articles.title: Google is working to fix two more frustrating Home bugs affecting routines and smart lights
articles.excerpt: Alarm routines can misfire, while some non-English light names stop working.
articles.body: TL;DR Some Google Clock alarm routines are opening Assistant settings instead of the routine editor or failing to run after an alarm. Google says it is aware of the problem and is working on a fix, while also investigating fresh timer complaints. Separately, Google says a fix for voice control of lights with non-English names should arrive within 24–48 hours. Smart speakers earn their keep in the little moments: turning off a light from bed, setting a kitchen timer, or launching a morning routine when your alarm goes off. You barely notice how useful that is until a basic command suddenly goes nowhere. Google Home has had several of those moments lately, from broken TV automations to weird accent glitches , and now users are reporting a fresh round of trouble with alarms and routines.

articles.title: What does a JWT actually prove? Less than your API assumes
articles.excerpt: View source on one of our generated widgets and you can find a tenant id, a connector handle and the address of a token issuer. Take those values to a terminal and you can obtain a valid token. Nobody…
articles.body: View source on one of our generated widgets and you can find a tenant id, a connector handle and the address of a token issuer. Take those values to a terminal and you can obtain a valid token. Nobody has stolen a signing key. The issuer is doing what it was built to do. I run backend engineering at GoodBarber , where we are testing an AI extension builder. Its widgets call third-party APIs through a proxy that holds the real API keys. The feature is a prototype serving a handful of pilot tenants; the design below is still evolving. The token tells the proxy which tenant the issuer accepted a request for. It does not identify the person making the call. That distinction determines what we can safely authorize, and it leaves a residual risk that a signature cannot remove.

articles.title: AI Agents Don't Fail When They Think. They Fail When Reality Changes.
articles.excerpt: An AI agent can make a perfectly reasonable decision and still do the wrong thing. That sounds like a model problem at first. Maybe the prompt was unclear. Maybe the model misunderstood the request. M…
articles.body: An AI agent can make a perfectly reasonable decision and still do the wrong thing. That sounds like a model problem at first. Maybe the prompt was unclear. Maybe the model misunderstood the request. Maybe the reasoning wasn't good enough. But in production, there is another failure mode that is much more interesting. Sometimes the agent was right when it made the decision. The problem is that reality changed before the agent acted on it . A payment that was pending failed. An available product went out of stock. A customer who was eligible for a refund submitted another request. A security policy changed while the agent was processing an operation. Another service, user, or agent modified the state that the first agent was relying on. The model didn't necessarily misunderstand anything.

articles.title: Recognizing ASL Letters with CNN and Ensemble Learning
articles.excerpt: Sign language uses hand shapes and movements to share information, but a computer can't understand these signs just by looking at a picture. We picked this topic to find out how AI identifies differen…
articles.body: Sign language uses hand shapes and movements to share information, but a computer can't understand these signs just by looking at a picture. We picked this topic to find out how AI identifies different hand shapes and if using a more advanced model is always better than using simpler techniques. In this project, we looked at different models to see which one works best for recognizing ASL letters. Our aim was to test a basic model, two techniques that combine multiple models, and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) all on the same set of data. Dataset and preprocessing We used the Sign Language MNIST dataset, which contains 27,455 training images and 7,172 test images. Each image is 28 × 28 pixels in grayscale.

articles.title: Firestore Security Rules: Deny by Default, Then Open the Narrowest Hole
articles.excerpt: Every few months someone opens an issue on a Firebase project along the lines of "your API key is exposed in the JavaScript bundle." It isn't a vulnerability, and the panic is misplaced — but the inst…
articles.body: Every few months someone opens an issue on a Firebase project along the lines of "your API key is exposed in the JavaScript bundle." It isn't a vulnerability, and the panic is misplaced — but the instinct behind it is right, just aimed at the wrong thing. A Firebase Web API key is a project identifier, not a credential. It's supposed to be public. What people are actually reaching for when they panic about it is the real question: if anyone can point a Firestore client at my project, what stops them reading everything and writing whatever they like? The answer is one file.

articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. Building a user-facing AI assistant interface is no longer just about wiring up a useState for the chat log and calling an LLM API. In 2024, the bar for what constit…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . Building a user-facing AI assistant interface is no longer just about wiring up a useState for the chat log and calling an LLM API. In 2024, the bar for what constitutes a 'production-grade' chat application has shifted dramatically. With the rise of sophisticated prompt injection attacks, the handling of Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and the stringent requirements of security frameworks like OWASP Top 10 for AI, frontend engineers are now effectively part of the security operations team. The challenge is bridging the gap between the rapid prototyping speed offered by UI libraries (like Vercel's assistant-ui ) and the strict, audited security standards required by enterprise compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001).

articles.title: Data privacy isn’t just for nerds — here’s why you should care too
articles.excerpt: The more I see how my personal data is used across services, the more I want to guard my privacy.
articles.body: A lot of times when I’ve mentioned moving to more privacy-focused apps and services, the reaction is more than a shrug — it’s a declaration that online privacy isn’t all that important. Most recently, at a tech event, I mentioned moving to Brave to avoid Google’s data collection and targeted advertising, and another attendee said that it’s just not important to them. That’s when I realized that there’s this general misunderstanding that prioritizing data privacy is the pastime of nerds and those prone to donning tin foil hats. I know I was someone who used to take a more laissez-faire approach to my online privacy. Years later, after grappling with the consequences of this, I feel that data privacy and data collection should be something everyone cares about.

articles.title: NASA Selects Far-Infrared Telescope as First in New Mission Class
articles.excerpt: NASA announced Wednesday a mission to explore the history and evolution of the universe, PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics), is advancing to the next phase of development. This space…
articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA announced Wednesday a mission to explore the history and evolution of the universe, PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics), is advancing to the next phase of development. This space telescope is the first in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions, called Probe Explorers, within the agency’s longstanding Explorers Program. “The PRIMA mission is humanity’s next window into the deep universe. It will unveil the obscure across cosmic time to better understand the formation of planets, stars, black holes, and even how water on Earth came to be,” said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington.

articles.title: NASA Aircraft to Make Low-Altitude Research Flights Over Colorado
articles.excerpt: Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammoni…
articles.body: A photo of the Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft, which will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Greeley, Colorado, to measure emissions in October 2026. Dynamic Aviation Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammonia, particulates, and other pollutants rising from agricultural lands and animal farms and the interaction with the Earth’s atmosphere. The mission is jointly led by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland; Colorado State University; and Boston University.  The Colorado deployment is the first series of flights for the FarmFlux mission.
